title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment that tests whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations versus blind repair. Using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates (preregistration vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1), we planned 40 confirmatory task pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid). Baseline (blind repair) passed the combined verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) passed in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11=29, n10=9 (guarded-only), n01=1 (baseline-only), n00=0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); exact two-sided paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used declared model gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode traces required to compute it are archived and the reproducibility path is documented in Methods. We bound conclusions to the synthetic controlled-fault bank, single declared model, and archived deterministic verifier/simulator and release the full artifact bundle for independent reaggregation.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to assist network operations (NetOps) with tasks that range from intent-to-configuration translation to automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a candidate configuration is checked by a deterministic verifier and, if violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior controlled evaluations in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings report that interposing deterministic verifiers and exposing diagnostics to repair models can raise verifier-detected pass rates while introducing new failure modes and interaction costs [1]–[4]. Surveys and field studies for NetOps caution that read-oriented usefulness does not imply safe closed-loop autonomy without conservative verification and orchestration [5].

Motivation and research question. The literature contains limited controlled evidence that quantifies verifier-guided repair behavior on vendor CLI configuration templates under deterministic, preregistered faults. A design-validity challenge is intervention informativeness: diagnostics can only improve outcomes when initial candidates trigger actionable verifier diagnostics. We therefore preregistered a deterministic controlled-fault injection and a paired shared-candidate design to ensure the intervention was meaningfully exercised. Our research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair for preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work:
Work on generate–verify–repair (GVR) spans program repair, IaC, and DSL tasks. Convergent generate–verify–repair architectures show verifier-interposed repair raises mechanically-checkable pass rates in code/IaC benchmarks and motivates verifier-guided repair loops [1]. Recent IaC-focused evaluations demonstrate verifier-first strategies and diagnostic exposure can materially improve verifier pass@1 and reduce specific verifier-detected failure classes under controlled budgets [2]. Controlled analyses have also revealed verifier-exploitation pathologies in iterative refinement: optimizing toward a single verifier proxy can reduce true target fidelity unless mitigations are applied [3]. Empirical studies of verifier-mediated agents document a measurable "verifier tax"—additional interaction horizons, compute and latency—requiring operational tradeoff analysis [4]. Finally, NetOps/AIOps surveys and demonstration-network case studies emphasize that LLMs are useful in read-oriented tasks but that closed-loop change automation requires rigorous verification and conservative orchestration [5].

Taken together, these strands justify a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment that (a) uses deterministic verifiers, (b) ensures intervention activation via outcome-independent fault injection, (c) adopts shared initial-candidate pairing semantics matching the estimand, and (d) archives per-episode traces and harm-labeling mappings for auditable safety aggregation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a binary success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and simulator-based compliance agreement. The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Design, adapter semantics, and pairing. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index one deterministic controlled-fault candidate (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) was generated and reused unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one shared initial generation and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic verifier diagnostics exposed. The adapter-mandated confirmatory task_count was fixed at 40.

Model configuration and sampling records. The declared model in the archived model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini and the archived temperature field is null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Per-call sampling parameters and hosted-model-call metadata (model-call timestamps, per-call runtime sampling records and provider traces) are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl) and can be inspected to reconstruct per-call sampling behavior. Execution accounting (planned and used model calls) appears in the execution manifest (model_calls_used = 118; maximum_model_calls = 120).

Controlled-challenge sampling, scoring rules, and harmful-change mapping. To ensure intervention activation we preregistered deterministic controlled faults (indices 1..40) that inject realistic actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change). The primary success predicate required both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator agreement. The preregistered harmful-change mapping used in scoring labels an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; this mapping was frozen and archived as a transformation artifact (execution/transformation_manifest.json) and per-episode validator traces are archived at execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl. The confirmatory analysis executor that produced the primary paired result did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the reproducibility path to compute that aggregation from archived artifacts is documented in Results.

Analysis plan. The primary test is an exact two-sided paired binary test (McNemar exact or equivalent). Reported outputs: discordant-pair counts, absolute paired risk difference, exact two-sided p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Missingness handling followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule: exclude a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; a sensitivity analysis treating missing episodes as failures is available in the archived artifacts. All raw per-episode artifacts and provider traces are archived for independent recomputation (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Timestamps and full execution manifest entries are archived (started_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:16:50.730326+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-09-04T21:19:34.370550+00:00).

Primary confirmatory outcome (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The archived pair table and CSV are analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (artifact hash recorded in the evidence bundle).

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under 'complete_pair_primary' because its source-generation was invalid/unscorable (both_missing_pairs = 1). The per-episode terminal error reasons are available in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation: status and reproducibility path. The preregistration specified a confirmatory safety hypothesis constraining harmful-overrepair (absolute increase <= 5%). The archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute this preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). Because the preregistered aggregation is not present in the archived confirmatory summary, we do not present a retroactive confirmatory safety claim. However, all required inputs to compute the preregistered aggregation are archived: per-episode validation_after.violation_codes are present in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl, and the frozen harmful-change mapping is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json. Independent auditors can deterministically reproduce the preregistered harmful-overrepair paired statistic by (1) iterating the 39 complete pairs, (2) applying the archived harmful-change rule (label episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE), and (3) computing paired counts and the preregistered paired test per the analysis plan. We therefore treat the confirmatory harmful-overrepair verdict as unresolved in this manuscript while providing the exact artifact paths needed for deterministic reproduction.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The preregistered paired result shows a substantial improvement in verifier+simulator-validated success when deterministic verifier diagnostics are exposed to the repair model under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics. The shared-initial-candidate pairing isolates the effect of diagnostics because both arms received the same injected candidate and identical repair budgets; archived per-episode validator traces illustrate plausible repair mechanisms (diagnostic codes directing targeted edits that avoid protected-interface changes or restore required command sequences). These per-episode traces are available in execution/scoring/task-000***-*.json.

Safety boundary and unresolved confirmatory safety aggregation. Crucially, the preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair question remains unresolved because the archived confirmatory executor omitted that aggregation. The preregistered harmful-change rule (harmful if validation_after.violation_codes includes PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE) and per-episode traces are archived and sufficient for deterministic recomputation; until that recomputation is performed and recorded in the archive the safety verdict must remain open. We deliberately document the reproducibility path rather than retroactively report preregistered safety numbers produced outside the archived confirmatory summary.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The guarded workflow materially improved verifier-defined correctness on the synthetic controlled-fault bank but incurs interaction cost: archived instrument counts show hosted_model_call_event_count = 118 and stage_counts = {valid_source_generation: 40, blind_controlled_fault_repair: 39, validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair: 39}. These counts permit exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure, but operational cost–latency feasibility at NetOps scale requires larger-scale studies. Verifier coverage and false-negative modes remain critical: a verifier cannot improve what it cannot detect, and narrow verifier surfaces risk overfitting to detectable violation classes.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: runtime model sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset) and reuse of exactly one initial generation per pair limit claims about sampling determinism and preclude attributing effects to different first-pass generations. Construct validity: primary success depends on deterministic verifier+simplified simulator agreement; these are proxies for device correctness but may mismatch real device behavior. External validity: a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic task bank constrain generalization to diverse vendor equipment and naturalistic workloads. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 gives reasonable precision for the observed effect but limits per-fault-class inference; subgroup analyses are exploratory.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This result is bounded to the archived synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory analysis executor and therefore remains unresolved; all artifacts and the frozen harmful-change mapping needed to reproduce that preregistered aggregation are archived and available for deterministic recomputation. We release the artifact bundle to enable independent recomputation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies before operational adoption.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10); that immutable archive reference is provided rather than inlining the prompt. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Preregistered harmful-change mapping and reconstructability: the harmful-change rules were frozen and archived; the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is at execution/transformation_manifest.json and per-episode raw traces are at execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json. All per-episode traces, provider calls, and analysis artifacts required to reproduce primary and preregistered secondary aggregations are archived in the evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
